apiDocs.title: API Docs
apiDocs.subtitle: Integrate your systems with OpenWA over HTTP
apiDocs.baseUrlHint: The address other systems use to reach this server. Examples below update as you type.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.step1: Create and connect a session on the Sessions page (scan the QR code with the WhatsApp phone).
quickstart.step2: Create a dedicated API key for your system on the API Keys page, with the operator role.
quickstart.step3: Copy the session ID shown above. Every message endpoint is scoped to a session.
quickstart.step4: Call the API with the key in the X-API-Key header:

auth.title: Authentication
auth.intro: Every request to /api must carry an API key, in either of these headers:
auth.admin: Everything, including API key, plugin and infrastructure management.
auth.operator: Send messages, manage sessions and webhooks. Use this for integrations.
auth.tip: Use one key per calling system so it can be revoked on its own. Keep keys on the server side and never ship them in browser or mobile app code.

ids.title: Session and chat IDs
ids.session: The UUID of the WhatsApp session (pick it above or copy it from the Sessions page). The session must be in the ready state.
ids.personal: A person: country code + phone number, no '+', spaces or leading 0, followed by @c.us. 0901 234 567 in Vietnam becomes 84901234567@c.us.
ids.group: A group: the group ID followed by @g.us. List them with GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/groups.
ids.phoneTip: The recipient must have a WhatsApp account. Sending to a number without WhatsApp fails.

send.title: Sending messages
send.intro: All message endpoints are relative to
send.mediaIntro: Pass either a public url that the server can download, or the file as base64 together with its mimetype.

responses.title: Responses and errors
responses.intro: Successful responses wrap the result in data. Errors use the same envelope with success: false and an error object.
responses.e400: Invalid body, or the session is not started / not ready.
responses.e401: Missing, invalid or expired API key.
responses.e403: The key's role is not allowed to call this endpoint (for example a viewer sending messages).
responses.e404: Session, message or resource not found.
responses.e429: Rate limit exceeded. Wait and retry with backoff.
responses.e500: Unexpected server error. Check the Logs page; the message may or may not have been sent.

webhooks.title: Receiving messages (webhooks)
webhooks.intro: To receive incoming WhatsApp messages, register an HTTPS endpoint of your system as a webhook for the session (or use the Webhooks page):
webhooks.events: Currently the server delivers the message.received event. Other event names are accepted when registering but are not emitted yet.
webhooks.verifyIntro: When a secret is set, X-OpenWA-Signature is an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body. Verify it before trusting the payload:
webhooks.ruleFast: Reply with a 2xx status quickly and do heavy work asynchronously; slow or failing responses are retried.
webhooks.ruleRetry: Failed deliveries are retried up to retryCount times, so the same event can arrive more than once.
webhooks.ruleIdempotent: Use idempotencyKey to detect and skip duplicates.

limits.title: Limits and good practice
limits.rate: Rate limit per client IP: 10 requests/second, 100/minute and 1000/hour (configurable with RATE_LIMIT_* variables).
limits.bulk: For many recipients, use send-bulk instead of a tight loop: it queues messages with a delay between them, which lowers the risk of WhatsApp banning the number.
limits.session: Only message people who expect it. Unsolicited bulk messaging gets numbers banned by WhatsApp.
limits.network: In Docker the ports are bound to 127.0.0.1. To let systems on other servers call the API, put a reverse proxy (Nginx, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel...) with HTTPS in front of the dashboard port and use that address as the Base URL.
